table.title: Mathematical Notation Reference
table.html:
SymbolNameLaTeXMeaning
∑Summation\sumDenotes the sum of a sequence of terms; an index and lower and upper bounds are usually written below and above the sign, as in ∑i=1n ai.
∫Integral\intRepresents an integral, used for antiderivatives and for definite integrals that accumulate a quantity over an interval or region; limits of integration may be attached to the sign.
∇Nabla\nablaA vector differential operator that produces the gradient of a scalar field and, depending on how it is combined with a vector field, the divergence or curl.
⊗Tensor product\otimesDenotes the tensor product of vector spaces or modules, or the Kronecker product of matrices; the intended construction is usually indicated by the surrounding context.
ℵ₀Aleph-null\aleph_0The cardinality of countably infinite sets such as the natural numbers; it is the smallest infinite cardinal number in standard set theory.
table.brief: Math notation table: Symbol (∑, ∫, ∇, ⊗, ℵ₀) / Name / LaTeX (like \otimes) / Meaning (long)

understanding.purpose: A reference for matching mathematical symbols with their names, LaTeX commands and meanings.
understanding.reading: Readers scan the symbol or name to find an entry, then read across the row for its command and explanation. Wrapping in the descriptions can be absorbed by the row height while the shorter identifiers remain easy to scan.
groups: Symbol, Name and LaTeX identify the same notation in different forms; they should remain easy to compare across rows.
Meaning contains explanatory prose and benefits from a wider, flexible measure.
keep_intact: Individual words in names and meanings where possible

preferred.name: r1C
preferred.note: Test a wider reading measure for Meaning while keeping Name compact. The 420px total costs 61px of horizontal scrolling but may substantially reduce row height.

acceptable.name: r1B
acceptable.note: Use a middle-width Meaning column to improve prose rhythm over r0B while limiting overflow to 25px.

acceptable.name: r2A
acceptable.note: Give Meaning 10px more than r1A to improve prose rhythm while keeping overflow between r1A and r1C.

acceptable.name: r2B
acceptable.note: Explore a wider prose measure to reduce row height further, accepting more horizontal scrolling while preserving all identifiers.

acceptable.name: r3A
acceptable.note: Use a Meaning width between r2A and r2B to improve prose wrapping while limiting overflow to 65px. Keep the identifier columns at their intact-word widths.

acceptable.name: r3B
acceptable.note: Give Meaning the minimum width needed for its longest word. The table overflows by 16px, preserving words with much less sideways travel, though explanations will remain tall.

acceptable.name: r3C
acceptable.note: Explore a wider prose measure to reduce row height and improve reading rhythm. The 125px overflow makes this a deliberate tradeoff for readers willing to scroll.

bad.name: r2C
bad.note: Fit within 359px to test the no-scroll alternative; Meaning will split its longest words and make rows taller.
bad.why: The narrow Meaning column splits words and stretches descriptions into as many as 18 lines, making rows difficult to scan despite fitting the viewport.

rationale: r1C keeps symbols, names and LaTeX commands intact while giving the long descriptions enough width to read in manageable blocks. Its 61px horizontal overflow requires a sideways scroll to see complete meanings, but preserves more useful prose width than the near-fitting alternatives. The narrow identifier columns remain visually grouped, while the wider Meaning column reflects its different job.

general: Allocate width according to each column's role and content, preserving identifiers and avoiding mid-word breaks.
Judge horizontal scrolling against the reading cost of narrow, deeply wrapped cells.
specific: Meaning contains much longer prose than the other columns and benefits most from additional width.
The first three columns already fit their longest unbreakable content at 75px, 99px and 80px.

tradeoffs: Wider meanings reduce wrapping and vertical travel but put more text beyond the initial viewport; narrower meanings keep more of each row visible at first sight but require more line changes.
uncertain: A designer might prefer r2B or r3C for more comfortable prose, or r2A for less horizontal scrolling. The ranges are conservative estimates around r1C, not independently rendered guarantees; they describe small independent adjustments with the other columns held near their preferred widths.

critique.good: The table fits within the viewport, the headers and identifiers remain intact, and each row is clearly separated.
critique.problems: The explanations form a very narrow, uneven column with frequent short lines and two split words. Tall rows leave large empty areas under the identifiers and make comparison between entries slow.
critique.cause: Meaning has only 84px of text width at a 105px column width, less than its 100px longest word. The other three columns together take 254px.

critique.good: The 121px Meaning column keeps words intact and reduces row heights while preserving readable headers and identifiers. The 16px overflow is modest.
critique.problems: The prose remains a narrow stack, and the right edge of many lines falls outside the initial viewport. Tensor product wraps, though it remains easy to understand.
critique.cause: Meaning has exactly 100px of text width, enough for its longest word but still a short measure for prose. The 376px total places its last 16px beyond the viewport.

critique.good: The wider Meaning column gives descriptions a better rhythm and noticeably shorter rows. The wider Name column keeps Tensor product on one line, and all identifiers remain intact.
critique.problems: A substantial part of the explanations lies beyond the initial viewport, so readers must scroll to read across each row. The extra width in Name competes with Meaning for space.
critique.cause: The 422px total exceeds the viewport by 62px. Name grows from 99px to 126px, pushing the start of Meaning farther right as well as increasing the total width.

critique.good: Symbols, names, commands, and headers remain intact. Multiword names wrap naturally, and the 35px overflow is modest.
critique.problems: Meaning is broken into many short lines, making rows tall and leaving large empty areas beneath the identifiers. The right side of the prose still requires scrolling.
critique.cause: The 140px Meaning column leaves 119px for text, while the first three columns occupy 254px.

critique.good: All identifiers and words remain intact, and its 25px overflow is the smallest of the three.
critique.problems: The descriptions form especially narrow, tall blocks, weakening the connection between entries and making vertical scanning laborious. The modest scroll saving still leaves the ends of lines outside the viewport.
critique.cause: Reducing Meaning to 130px leaves only 109px for text, increasing wrapping and row heights.

critique.good: The wider descriptions read more naturally and produce substantially shorter rows; identifiers remain intact and easy to scan.
critique.problems: A sizeable portion of each description lies beyond the initial viewport, so readers must scroll sideways to read complete lines. The empty space below short identifiers remains conspicuous.
critique.cause: The 166px Meaning column improves the text measure but increases total overflow to 61px; the first three columns still consume 254px.

critique.good: All headers, symbols, commands and individual words remain intact. The modest horizontal overflow preserves more room for prose than the viewport-width design.
critique.problems: The explanations form tall, narrow blocks, leaving large empty areas in the identifier columns. Readers must scroll sideways to read the ends of lines.
critique.cause: The 150px Meaning column provides only 129px for text, while the first three columns consume 254px.

critique.good: The wider prose measure produces more readable explanations and shorter rows. Identifiers and individual words remain intact.
critique.problems: The table extends 85px beyond the viewport, so a substantial portion of every explanation requires horizontal scrolling. Tall rows still leave visible empty space beneath the short identifiers.
critique.cause: The 190px Meaning column improves wrapping but raises the total width to 445px; the first three columns still occupy 254px.

critique.good: The whole table fits at first sight, and the identifiers and headers are easy to scan.
critique.problems: The explanations become very narrow, producing exceptionally tall rows and large empty areas in the other columns. Two words split mid-word, interrupting reading.
critique.cause: The 105px Meaning column leaves only 84px for text, less than the 100px needed for its longest unbreakable word.

review.method: two fresh-context blind reviews; letters shuffled; includes browser auto layout and equal widths as neutral references

r2C.why: The whole table fits, and the symbols, names and LaTeX remain easy to scan. The narrow Meaning column produces very tall rows and splits words such as “antiderivatives” and “construction”.

r1B.why: The identifying columns stay intact, and Meaning has enough room for more natural wrapping. A small amount of horizontal scrolling is needed to read the ends of lines.

r1C.why: The wider Meaning column makes the descriptions easier to read and shortens the rows, but much of each description lies beyond the initial viewport, requiring sustained horizontal scrolling.

ref_equal.why: Although it fits the viewport, it splits “Summation” and many words in Meaning across lines. The narrow descriptions make the rows exceptionally tall and difficult to scan.

r2A.why: The descriptions wrap more naturally than in the layouts that fit, but a substantial part of Meaning lies beyond the viewport. Reading the definitions requires horizontal scrolling.

ref_auto.why: The identifiers remain clear and Meaning wraps mostly at word boundaries. Only a little extends beyond the viewport, though the descriptions are still narrow and the rows tall.

raw.unsure: The screenshots do not show the full right edge of the wider layouts, so the exact scrolling distance for each is uncertain. B and F are close; B gives the descriptions a little more room at the cost of slightly more scrolling.

ref_equal.why: The narrow Name and Meaning columns split words repeatedly, while the very tall rows leave large empty areas in the other columns.

r2C.why: The identifiers fit within the viewport, but Meaning is cramped and splits words such as “antiderivatives” and “construction.”

r1B.why: Names and commands stay intact, and Meaning has enough room for more natural wrapping. Its right edge requires a small amount of horizontal scrolling.

r2A.why: The wider Meaning column reads more comfortably, but more of each line lies beyond the viewport, making sideways scrolling necessary to read the descriptions.

ref_auto.why: The compact identifier columns and modestly widened Meaning column preserve words with relatively little horizontal scrolling, though descriptions still wrap frequently.

r1C.why: The wide Meaning column gives the prose a better measure, but a substantial part of nearly every line lies beyond the viewport, increasing the cost of reading across rows.

raw.unsure: The exact amount of horizontal scrolling is difficult to judge from the images; C and E are close, depending on how much weight is given to shorter lines versus viewport fit.

provenance.note: AI visual design judgement; not a human reading study

amends.reason: changed after the holdout freeze (re-review or redesign); the frozen record stays canonical
